doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Sun Ra's last years and the estate
title: Intestacy, Alton Abraham's death and leaving the Sun Ra catalog
summary: The deaths of Sun Ra and Abraham left chaos over masters and rights, and Gordon walked away.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Wow. And you mentioned he died intestate and obviously any business details you don’t want to go into but what kind of impact did that have for you in terms of remitting royalties or whatever it was?

Well you know there’s always an estate. You have to pay your royalties whether a person is alive or dead there’s always — you always have to pay someone and that didn’t free us from our obligations to pay. But what was sad, well first of all what was sad was that we were at the end of the deal when Alton Abraham had died. And we were negotiating a deal for more, more releases. You know I was trying to do another ten Sun Ra records and negotiating that with Alton Abraham and then he died and that ended — that really ended my opportunity to continue to work with Sun Ra’s music because there was a lot of chaos after Sun Ra died, Alton died, you know, who did you negotiate with now, where are the masters, who is in charge, a lot of people said, “Oh he’s dead here’s an opportunity.” There was a lot of people wanting to buy the catalog, license the catalog, control the catalog, control their estates for others, and because of the intestate situation that was my cue to finally say good-bye to that whole thing. I didn’t want — you know there’s a word in Yiddish — tsuris — and that word means heartaches and you know the stuff that you know burns out your — gives you ulcers. I didn’t want the tsuris of being involved in this free-for-all of Sun Ra’s masters and stuff.
Yeah I can certainly understand, especially given the very congenial and warm personal dealings you’d had with them it sounds like, to go into that feeding frenzy would have been terrible.
